text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- The Supreme Court observed that the elections set for February 3 could not be postponed for holding of census.
- Supreme Court Chief Justice Sajjad Ali Shah said only parliament could undo the Eighth Amendment giving the president power to dissolve the assembly,
- The caretaker government will convene a meeting of five major political parties to brief them about the latest talks with the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund.
- A spokesman of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Resources ruled out any cut in domestic prices of petroleum products as a result of Iraq's re-entry into the oil market.

- Pakistan's major bilateral donors, including Japan and Canada, have taken exception to World Bank attempts to force Pakistan to slash even the core projects of other donors simply to protect the Bank-aided projects from being affected by a 21-billion-rupee cut in this year's development budget.
- Employees of state-run Pakistan Telecommunication Co Ltd in Lahore observed a complete strike for the second consecutive day in protest at the murder of a trade union leader.

- The Privatisation Commission has completed a regulatory framework to privatise Pakistan International Airlines, Pakistan Railways, airports, Pakistan Telecommunication Co Ltd, banks and a couple of other state enterprises in the next 50 days.
- The caretaker government has cancelled employment contracts of 37 retired military officers re-employed as civil servants by the previous government in violation of rules.
- Pakistan will import 540,000 tonnes of wheat from the U.S. and Australia to bridge the gap between output and consumption.

- A list of bank loan defaulters containing 12,000 to 15,000 names will be released on Monday or Tuesday after the government issues an ordinance to amend the Fidelity and Secrecy Clause of the Banks Act, 1974, sources said.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The government plans to get specialised agencies to pursue cases of flight of unearned and ill-gotten wealth to offshore islands and other tax-free zones, President Farooq Leghari said.
The Karachi Stock Exchange has selected 32 state-owned firms for listing with five to one percent share offering to the public.

- Pakistan expects to reduce inflation to eight to nine percent in calendar 1997 from about 12 percent now under a reform programme being negotiated with the IMF, Shahid Javed Burki, economic advisor to the prime minister, said.
THE NATION

- A local court released on bail Naheed Khan, political secretary to ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto, saying providing relief to victims of terrorism was no crime. Khan was charged of giving money from Baitul Ma'al (state funds for poor and needy) to 55 people.
THE NEWS
- Arif Habib has been elected as the president of Karachi Stock Exchange for a second consecutive term.
- Former chairman of Rice Export Corporation of Pakistan, M.Ishaque, has been arrested by the Federal Investigation Agency for alleged involvement in a 20-million-rupee gunny bag scam.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
